main_body: Open wooden shelving unit with three shelves of scrolls and items against a dark red-brown back wall, drawn almost straight from the front
top_band: Light tan band at rows 1-3, with a darker brown line at row 4 and a mid-brown outline at row 0. It is only about 3 rows and reads as a cap, not a surface.
evidence: In the middle column the order is a 3-row tan cap, then a dark row, then the frame and shelf interior down to the base. The cap is only 3 rows against a 27-row face and has no lighter front-edge line, so it works as a hat on an elevation. The shelf planks are 2-row bands drawn face-on, with no visible top surface. The inset dark back wall is a real recess, but the main body is still a front elevation with a thin top.

style.evidence: The wood has about 4 tones (light tan, mid tan, brown, dark brown), against 5-6 on the references. The outline is a dark brown tint, which is good. The dark back wall in each bay and the top band are large flat fills with no grain or speckle. The items are small and simple, so the tiles are mostly 3-5 colours, thinner than the reference stall and well.
